thesis: Management at Berkshire Hathaway looks disciplined and shareholder-aligned: capital returns are funded from operating cash flow, incentives reference multi-year targets and guidance has broadly been delivered. Insider activity is routine.
invalidation_rationale: Governance view: a dividend cut or a large debt-funded acquisition would break it.
conviction_reason: Long, verifiable record in filings; pay-mix detail not quantified.
self_evidence_reason: Proxy, annual report and Form 4 indexes reviewed.

sources.title: Proxy statements (DEF 14A) — BRK-B (SEC EDGAR filing index)
Insider transaction reports (Form 4) — BRK-B (SEC EDGAR filing index)
Annual reports (10-K) — BRK-B (SEC EDGAR filing index)

management_quality.assessment: Leadership has kept a consistent strategy around its low-cost insurance float and a decentralised operating model.

capital_allocation.assessment: Dividends and buybacks are funded from free cash flow; acquisitions are bolt-on rather than transformational.

incentives.assessment: Annual bonus and long-term awards reference earnings, cash flow and relative shareholder return targets.

insider_activity.assessment: Form 4 activity is dominated by award vesting and plan-based sales.

guidance_vs_delivery.assessment: Recent annual targets were broadly met; misses were flagged early.
